title: E2E acceptance criteria should be specific and testable, not vague assertions
description: Three acceptance criteria in Epic 2 scenarios lacked specificity: 'Tests are isolated' (what constitutes isolation?), 'Each service builds from its own Dockerfile' (doesn't verify multi-stage correctness), 'UI components from MUI library' (not testable as-is). Vague criteria produce weak or untestable E2E assertions.
root_cause: Phase 3.2 (Generate Phase E2E Config) derives acceptance criteria from blackbox specs but does not apply a testability filter. Criteria that describe properties ('tests are isolated') rather than observable behaviors ('each test uses isolated database state via transaction rollback') pass through unchecked.
recommendation: In Phase 3.2, when generating acceptance_criteria for each scenario, apply a testability check: each criterion must describe an observable behavior or measurable property (e.g., 'X returns Y', 'command exits with code 0', 'image size < N MB'). Flag and refine criteria that are property assertions without observable verification methods. Remove criteria that are code review concerns (e.g., 'uses library X') rather than runtime behaviors.
initiative_context: Janus Communication Surveillance Platform, Phase 1, 35 features, 5 epics
